input: {"focus":"Evolve the shared-ui StatusBadge presentation primitive and its tests so callers may optionally select neutral, positive, warning, or critical tone; rendered markup always exposes the effective tone through data-tone while status-label behavior remains unchanged, and bind both supplied acceptance scenarios.","currentUnderstanding":"collection-review/workspace/shared-ui already owns and exposes StatusBadge and StatusBadgeProps (tagged ui/browser) from src/status-badge.tsx. The props currently contain ReviewStatus status plus optional label; rendering emits a span with class status-badge and data-status, and displays either the supplied label or the existing Passed/Failed default. There is no tone contract or data-tone today. Existing Vitest coverage renders static markup under Node and verifies default labels and data-status/custom-label independence. The plan therefore appears implementable entirely in this owner by adding a constrained optional tone prop, resolving omission to neutral only for markup, and retaining the existing label computation. The two generated Cucumber scenarios are still pending, and src/tests/steps does not yet exist; the declared Cucumber configuration will load this module's .ts/.tsx step definitions once provided. The ordinary API view confirms ReviewStatus is available from contracts, while the ordinary and test views have limited coverage (1 and 2 respectively), so their omissions are not evidence that other interfaces do not exist.","questions":["Whether the four-value tone vocabulary should be a separately named/exported type or an inline union on StatusBadgeProps is not dictated by the supplied requirements; this should be decided during organization based on keeping the public contract clear without expanding exports unnecessarily.","The exact Cucumber step-state pattern is not established by this module because it currently has no step definitions; implementation can use a small scenario-local World/state in the new binding unless later evidence or checks require shared test support.","The API views are coverage-limited, so no claim should be made that unobserved interfaces are unavailable; none appears necessary for the straightforward local implementation currently envisioned."]}
